name: A solo balance actor fights its own balance_spawn enemies without a raid group
contract: solo: true drives the actor the way DriveRaidBot drives a raid bot (melee positioning, auto-attack, CastRotation) but with no tank gate and no boss encounter: candidates come from whoever the player (or a unit it owns) is already in combat with. role selects melee positioning as for a raid bot; rotation_assist with specialization 1 (Barbarian, CoARotationData.h) resolves to Ancestral Strike 801576, the only rotation spell the fixture teaches, so a cast proves the solo driver reached CastRotation on its own, outside DriveRaidBots' boss-only path. SpawnBalanceEnemies now sends each spawn's own AI to attack the owner (CreatureAI::AttackStart) right after it joins the map, so the fight starts deterministically instead of depending on proximity aggro from a relocation event the fixture never sends. The two balance_spawn Scarlet Soldiers (4286) are an ordinary elite melee entry (rank 1, creature_template) forced to level 30 by balance_spawn/CoAGameplayTestBalanceLevels; with CoA dungeon scaling applied to them and no armor on the bare level-40 fixture beyond its single weapon, the fixture's set_health gives it a large health pool so the regression proves the driver engages, kills and switches targets rather than measuring real class balance (the catalog in later tasks supplies real gear).

steps.label: Let spawn AI and local level scaling settle
SETUP: the fighter knows its only rotation spell
The first balance-spawned Scarlet Soldier dies to the unassisted solo driver
The solo driver switches to the second Scarlet Soldier and kills it too
The solo actor cast its rotation spell without a raid encounter or boss
The fighter survives soloing two elites
